sections.h2: Which county bills my Kansas City, Missouri property tax?
sections.html:
It depends on which side of the city your house is on. Kansas City covers about 319 square miles across four counties: Jackson, Clay, Platte and Cass (Wikipedia). The city does not send its own bill. Its finance page says every taxable parcel is assessed by the county assessor and the city levy appears on the county bill.

  • Jackson County: Collection Department, 816-881-3232. Most of the older core and south side falls here.
  • Clay County: Collector, 816-407-3200, 1 Courthouse Square, Liberty.
  • Platte and Cass counties: look up the county collector on that county's official site, using your parcel number or address.

Check the county shown on your last bill before you call anyone. A wrong call costs time when a closing date is close.

sections.h2: What does Kansas City's own levy look like?
sections.html:
The city lists five levies, each stated per $100 of assessed valuation. The 2024 combined figure on the finance page is $1.5291 for city purposes. School, county, library and other districts bill separately on the same county statement, so ask the collector for the full rate on your parcel.

City of Kansas City levies, tax year 2024 (kcmo.gov finance page)

Missouri assesses residential property at 19 percent of true value, agricultural land at 12 percent, other real property at 32 percent and personal property at 33 1/3 percent. Each county assessor adjusts real property values in odd-numbered years, so a new reassessment lands in 2027.

sections.h2: What does Kansas City look like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Kansas City is the largest city in Missouri by population and area, built where the Kansas and Missouri rivers meet. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts give 521,220 residents for 2025 and 221,979 households. Owners hold 55.4% of homes. The median owner-occupied value is $242,900, median gross rent is $1,238 and median household income is $69,166.

No single school district covers the city. About 15 separate districts serve it, so the district on a bill matters when you compare two houses a few blocks apart. The economy leans on federal offices, a Federal Reserve bank, the IRS service center, health and animal science research and agriculture companies.

Weather is part of the picture for any house here. The city sits in Tornado Alley, and it has had ice storms and river flooding. Roofs, basements and drainage are the items a buyer's inspector tends to check, and a seller with deferred repairs and an unpaid tax bill can find both come up together.

sections.h2: When is Jackson County property tax due, and how do I pay?
sections.html:
The 2026 bill is due in full by December 31, 2026. The county's Board of Equalization FAQ adds that recalculations for 2026 appeal decisions are suspended until January 2027, so the bill still has to be paid on time. Any refund is then issued automatically, and paying under protest is not required to get one.

  • In person: Jackson County Courthouse, 415 E 12th Street in Kansas City, or the Truman Courthouse, 112 W Lexington Avenue in Independence, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday.
  • Drop boxes at both courthouses close at midnight on December 31. Cash does not go in them.
  • By mail to the Jackson County Collector. The postmark must be December 31 or earlier.
  • Online at payments.jacksongov.org. E-check costs $1.25. Cards cost 2.75% of the bill, and a $2 per transaction fee applies, all kept by the processor.

The county accepts partial payments on real property, but only in person or by mail. Interest, penalties and fees accrue on the unpaid part after December 31. Seniors may split the county bill into four equal installments without penalty through the Senior Quad Payment Program, and the Collection Department can say whether your account qualifies.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Jackson County assessment?
sections.html:
The 2026 appeal deadline to the county Board of Equalization was July 13, 2026, and it has passed. For a notice or print summary of values, call the Real Property Assessment Department at 816-881-3530 or email tpaASMT@jacksongov.org.

After the board rules, you can appeal to the Missouri State Tax Commission, which has its own online process. Two points from the board's FAQ matter. Signing a stipulated value from the Assessment Department cancels the board appeal and ends any Commission appeal. A withdrawal must be in writing, and the board's mailing address is 1300 Washington, Kansas City, MO 64106.

Taxes paid under protest follow Missouri statute 139.031: full payment on time plus a written statement of grounds and the claimed fair market value. The county sends protest payments to Attn: Protest, P.O. Box 219747, Kansas City, MO 64121-9747. Protest funds are released every other month, so a refund tied to a value change usually comes faster without it.

sections.h2: What if my Kansas City house sits in Clay County?
sections.html:
Clay County's Collector says tax bills normally go out by mid-November, and an owner who has not received one by November 30 should call 816-407-3200. Missouri law requires payment by December 31 whether or not a bill arrives.

A payment postmarked after December 31 draws a one-time 9% penalty and interest of 1.5% per month on the unpaid balance. Clay County asks owners not to rely on bank bill-pay services, since those payments often reach the office without a postmark and are posted by the date on the check. Debit cards and e-check are free to Clay County customers, and credit cards carry a 2.45% fee.

sections.h2: How should I handle a tax bill when selling a Kansas City house?
sections.html:
Start with the county, parcel number and bill year. The title company asks the collector for the amount owed and pays it at closing. If a house has an old year unpaid plus a current bill, getting the payoff in writing before you sign anything avoids surprises on the settlement statement.

A homeowner who owes back tax and has repairs to make can also sell the house as-is for cash. In that case the title company pays the tax from the proceeds, as it would in any other sale.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax for a house in Kansas City, Missouri?
faqs.a: The county where the parcel sits. Kansas City spans Jackson, Clay, Platte and Cass counties, and the city's levy is added to the county bill rather than billed separately.

faqs.q: When is the 2026 Kansas City tax bill due?
faqs.a: December 31, 2026. In Jackson County the drop boxes close at midnight that day and mailed payments need a postmark of that date or earlier.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my 2026 Jackson County value?
faqs.a: No. The Board of Equalization deadline was July 13, 2026. Call 816-881-3530 for a value summary and watch for the next reassessment in 2027.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay under protest to get a refund in Jackson County?
faqs.a: No. The county says refunds from a value change are issued automatically. Paying under protest can delay them, because protest funds are released every other month.

faqs.q: What is the Kansas City city property tax rate?
faqs.a: The city's combined 2024 levy was $1.5291 per $100 of assessed valuation. School and other district rates are added on the county bill, so ask your collector for the total on your parcel.
